subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw keep strict startup fail-fast for active SecretRefs, or add a bounded generic retry/degrade policy for side-effecting exec providers under supervisor restarts?
rationale: This changes how credential-provider failures behave at startup, which affects security posture, recovery UX, external service quotas, and whether existing deployments fail closed or wait/degrade.

options.title: Bounded generic startup retry
options.body: Add a narrow startup-only retry/backoff path with clear logs/docs and no provider-specific 1Password policy in core.

options.title: Strict fail-fast plus docs
options.body: Keep the current fail-fast runtime contract and document supervisor `RestartSec`/launchd throttling plus external resolver caching as the supported mitigation.

options.title: Broader degraded-startup design
options.body: Design a larger unavailable-secret state that can keep the gateway online while disabling only affected surfaces, with explicit security review first.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup retry
recommendation.body: Add a narrow startup-only retry/backoff path with clear logs/docs and no provider-specific 1Password policy in core.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail points most strongly to `joshavant` for the SecretRef runtime and resolver contract affected by the policy choice.
